content.text:
The best match is mp-1105121 (Ti8BiO7) alone. The fits leave a lot unexplained, so confidence is only moderate.

1. **Ti8BiO7 matches the main peak positions.** Its cell is equivalent to a C-centred orthorhombic cell of about 16.94 × 7.86 × 3.04 Å. By my hand calculation that cell has a d(200) reflection at about 8.47 Å (10.44°) and a d(110) reflection at about 7.13 Å (12.40°). These line up with the two strongest low-angle peaks in the pattern, at 10.45° and 12.4°.
2. **It is the only candidate that fits at all.** On its own, Ti8BiO7 gave an R-factor of 0.72. Every other single candidate I fitted (Cs2Ti(WO4)3, BaCaSmSbO6, RbNbO3, Ba2YFe3O8) scored between 0.955 and 0.977. I did not fit Mn(PtO2)3, Sr3Nd(FeO4)2, ZrGeO4 or TiCoO3 on their own; they appear only in the two-phase fits below.
3. **No second phase helps.** I added each of those four to Ti8BiO7 in turn. Each got 0 to 6% of the weight, and R stayed between 0.718 and 0.722.
4. **The leftover is mostly wrong peak heights, not missing peaks.** After the Ti8BiO7 fit there is still a large positive leftover at 12.4° (about 55 on the 100 scale) and smaller ones at 10.45° and 37.6°. There are negative dips near 32° and 38.6°. These sit at or near Ti8BiO7's own peaks, which points to intensity mismatches such as preferred orientation rather than another phase. I can't fully rule out a phase that isn't among the nine candidates.
